elements.element: No exclusivity or sole-supplier designation binding Customer
elements.evidence: "Vendor will be a non-exclusive provider of hosted analytics services"

elements.element: Customer retains freedom to source the same or similar services elsewhere (no de facto exclusivity elsewhere in the clause)
elements.evidence: "Customer may procure the same or similar services from any other supplier at any time"; 12.3 "Nothing restricts Customer from ... engaging any supplier"

elements.element: Any exclusivity limited to a defined product category
elements.evidence: No exclusivity survives: "a non-exclusive provider" — condition demonstrably absent
No exclusivity term remains after deletion of "sole and exclusive provider ... throughout the term"

elements.element: Exclusivity ends automatically on Vendor's failure to meet service levels or delivery dates
elements.evidence: No exclusivity obligation exists to terminate; clause is now "non-exclusive"

offending_extra_words: and Customer may procure the same or similar services from any other supplier at any time
reasons: The locked preferred level is achieved: the sole-and-exclusive appointment is converted to non-exclusive, so no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation binds Customer.

Minimality fails: the added trailing sentence duplicates protection already granted by untouched Section 12.3 ('Nothing restricts Customer from ... engaging any supplier'), and a tighter edit (deleting 'sole and exclusive' / inserting 'non-exclusive') suffices.
Official gates confirm over-expansion: 15 words to 26 words (ratio 1.73) and changed-character ratio 0.631, both above the permitted limits.
Intent is preserved: Section 12.3 and all other commercial terms remain effective, no undefined term or contradiction is introduced, and the prior conflict with 12.3 is resolved.
